trickyParts: suggestionsBehindLock runs the call on a one-connection store of its own (deps.Store.Pool.Config() with MaxConns 1, MinConns 0, MinIdleConns 0, wrapped in store.NewPool) and reads that connection's backend pid; the call's path runs one statement at a time, so that connection is the call's. The poll asks pg_locks, through the holder transaction, whether that pid waits on a lock the holder blocks.

Round 1 counted every backend the holder blocked; the issue create the tests seed schedules the spec's settlement (~20 ms later), which queues behind the same locks on asks and issues, so a call that never waited passed (sjawhar/legion#2217 review 5646588420).
The helper checks the answer channel before every poll and fails at once if the call answered first; once its backend waits it receives the answer with no timer (plan decision 2).
The lock transaction still runs on the test's shared pool; the call's pool is closed by a cleanup registered before the rollback's, so the rollback runs first.
deviations: Plan decision 3 ('the waiter is identified by the test's own lock') was not enough: round 2 also ties the waiter to the call's own backend through a dedicated one-connection pool. No SQL text is pinned.
